# Original-source screening

Run `uv venv --python python3.11 .venv-screen`, then `uv pip install --python .venv-screen/bin/python -r vendor/screening/requirements.txt` and `python3 scripts/setup-screening.py` from the repository root. The runtime is isolated from AutoShorts. Weights live in a persistent cache and are verified against pinned SHA256 digests; a missing/corrupt model blocks processing. Environment overrides are documented in `.env.example`.

The mandatory pipeline gate screens original media before cleaning, transcription, clipping and enrichment. It records the original SHA256, policy version, model hashes, coverage, scores and findings. Rejected and allowed results can be reused for identical original bytes under the same policy; uncertain results are re-evaluated. Changing thresholds, preprocessing or models requires a policy-version bump.

YAMNet is Google's published AudioSet classifier. Every audio stream and each of its channels is decoded separately to16kHzmono, preventing stereo phase cancellation and ignored secondary tracks, then classified in overlapping0.975s windows with0.48s hops. Music and Singing classes and their available ontology descendants are considered; class IDs come from the pinned AudioSet ontology rather than a contiguous index range. The separate `music-classes.json` data carries Google attribution and its CC BY-SA4.0 license; its SHA256 and the YAMNet vocabulary SHA256 are verified.0.20or higher rejects,0.05–0.20blocks as uncertain. These conservative initial thresholds are not calibrated precision/recall guarantees. A clean source can be blocked; quiet or unusual music can be missed. Dedicated validation remains required.

Visual inference normalizes display rotation without scrambling dimensions and decodes every primary-stream frame, sharing inference only for byte-identical consecutive frames. The YOLOX detector decodes individual person boxes. Every detected person must have one uniquely assigned, separately assessable face; small/occluded/crowded/ambiguous figures block. Face presentation classification does not establish gender identity. It cannot guarantee absence of female figures, especially drawings, reflections, tiny people or missed detections. A music rejection can stop before visual work; the result explicitly records that visual screening did not run. Visual timestamps currently use average frame rate and may be approximate for variable-frame-rate sources.

These checks are automated content screening, not a religious certification. No classifier can prove perfect absence. Candidate discovery is metadata-only and must never be represented as having passed these checks.

Model sources: https://github.com/tensorflow/models/tree/master/research/audioset/yamnet ; https://github.com/opencv/opencv_zoo/tree/main/models/object_detection_yolox ; https://github.com/onnx/models/tree/main/validated/vision/body_analysis/age_gender . Vendored YAMNet code preserves its Apache-2.0 license and exact source commit in `yamnet/PROVENANCE.md`.

Policy version3 invalidates earlier passes. Audio uses original-audio-v3 and visual uses unchanged original-visual-v2. The audio report includes the pinned class-selection hash; acceptance also checks per-channel duration agreement, plausible window coverage and unique stream layouts. Allowed cache reports require the exact audio/visual subpolicy versions and model hashes, per-channel coverage and every-frame counts. Legacy source-based assets cannot reach a new Postiz upload until their original passes current checks; confirmation polling for already-created posts remains read-only. Process termination cleans up active decoder children.

CPU benchmarking on this host measured approximately0.09seconds per representative1080pframe with2OpenCVthreads. This is not a throughput guarantee for arbitrary sources; long recordings can require hours. Default inference uses2threads (`SCREENING_CV_THREADS=1..16` override). Screening is bounded at12hours; affected pg-boss jobs expire after14hours, leaving room for other processing. Deployment throughput and resource acceptance remain outstanding.

The original-media gate stops after either rejected or uncertain audio. Visual screening is explicitly marked `not-run`; the source remains blocked. This avoids hours of unnecessary visual inference when audio alone already prevents approval. Allowed audio still requires every-frame visual coverage. Thresholds, model/preprocessing contracts and the set of acceptable media are unchanged, so the existing policy version remains valid.
